acts_cited_auto: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

acts_cited.act: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

facts_of_case: Petitioner's husband filed a petition under Section 13(1)(ia)(ib) of the Hindu Marriage Act. Petitioner seeks transfer to Dabwali court due to distance and difficulty in defending case.

legal_principles.principle: While deciding the transfer application, courts are required to give more weightage and consideration to the convenience of female litigants.
legal_principles.held: The Courts are required to give more weightage and consideration to the convenience of the female litigants and transfer of legal proceedings from one Court to another should ordinarily be allowed, taking into consideration their convenience and the Courts should desist from putting female litigants under undue hardships.
cited_cases: Sumita Singh Vs. Kumar Sanjay, (2002) SC 396
Rajani Kishor Pardeshi Vs. Kishor Babulal Pardeshi, (2005) (12) SCC 237

legal_principles.principle: Courts should consider the economic soundness of both parties, social strata of the spouses, and their behavioural pattern while exercising power under Section 24 of the Code of Civil Procedure.
legal_principles.held: The cardinal principle for exercise of power under Section 24 of the Code of Civil Procedure is that the ends of justice should demand the transfer of the suit, appeal or other proceeding. In matrimonial matters, wherever Courts are called upon to consider the plea of transfer, the Courts have to take into consideration the economic soundness of both the parties, the social strata of the spouses and their behavioural pattern, their standard of life prior to the marriage and subsequent thereto and the circumstances of both the parties in eking out their livelihood and under whose protective umbrella they are seeking their sustenance to life.
cited_cases: N.C.V. Aishwarya Vs. A.S. Saravana Karthik Sha, (2022) Live Law (SC) 627

outcome.final_order: Petition transferred to competent Court of jurisdiction at Dabwali, District Sirsa.
